newsitem.title: UK: IATA freight forecast sees 6.6pct growth to 2000.
newsitem.headline: IATA freight forecast sees 6.6pct growth to 2000.

text.p: World airfreight will grow at an annual average rate of 6.6 percent between 1996 and 2000, the International Air Transport Association (IATA) said in its latest world freight forecast.

In the annual five year forecast, due for release later this year, IATA said airfreight will grow 5.9 percent this year, rising to 7.5 percent in 1997, then by seven percent in 1998, 7.2 percent in 1999 and slipping to 5.3 percent in 2000.

Last year IATA forecast a 10.5 percent rise between 1995 and 1999. However this year's projection for the five years is tempered by the downturn in airfreight seen at end-1995 and early 1996, an IATA source told Reuters.

Airfreight tonnage carried is expected to rise to 14.13 million tonnes in 2000 from 10.88 million in 1996, a 37.6 percent increase over the period. Last year's tonnage stood at 10.3 million compared to 1994's revised 9.3 million.
The forecast is based on around 74 percent of total international scheduled and charter freight traffic, compared with nearly 72 percent previously, but does not include some major airlines.
It also excludes the U.S.-UK airfreight market, IATA added.
